title: Nearly half of seniors improve with age — and researchers think they know why
titleZh: 当你开始接受衰老时，身体会发生什么
summary:
人们常将衰老描述为一个持续走下坡路的过程，但一项最新研究发现，许多老年人的状态其实会随时间的推移而改善。耶鲁大学研究人员基于一项针对美国老年人、历时十余年且具全国代表性的调查数据发现，在65岁及以上人群中，近一半人在认知功能、身体功能，或二者同时出现了提升。

来源：福克斯新闻；作者：Khloe Quill；原文发布时间：2026-03-15 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Aging is often depicted as a steady decline, but new research suggests that many older adults actually improve over time. Using more than a decade of data from a large, representative study of older Americans, Yale University researchers found that nearly half of adults 65 and older showed improvement in cognitive function, physical function or both.
paragraphs.contentZh: 人们常将衰老描述为一个持续走下坡路的过程，但一项最新研究发现，许多老年人的状态其实会随时间的推移而改善。耶鲁大学研究人员基于一项针对美国老年人、历时十余年且具全国代表性的调查数据发现，在65岁及以上人群中，近一半人在认知功能、身体功能，或二者同时出现了提升。

paragraphs.contentEn: The improvements were consistent across the study population, and were linked to the participants' mindset about aging, according to a press release. "In contrast to a predominant belief or stereotype that age is a time of continuous and inevitable decline, we found evidence that a meaningful number of older persons actually show improvement over 12 years in cognitive and/or physical health," lead author Becca Levy, a professor of social and behavioral sciences at Yale, told Fox News Digital.
paragraphs.contentZh: 新闻稿指出，这种改善现象在研究涉及的不同人群中具有一致性，并与参与者对待衰老的心态有关。该研究的第一作者、耶鲁大学社会与行为科学教授贝卡·莱维在接受福克斯新闻数字版采访时表示：“与普遍认为衰老意味着持续且不可避免的衰退这种观点或刻板印象相反，我们的研究发现，在长达12年的时间里，有相当数量的老年人在认知健康和（或）身体健康方面出现了实际改善。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The research, which was published in the journal Geriatrics, relied on data from the Health and Retirement Study, a federally supported, long-running survey of older Americans. Researchers tracked changes in cognition using global performance tests and measured physical function based on walking speed, which was seen as a "vital sign" because of its strong links to disability, hospitalization and mortality.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这项研究发表于《老年医学》期刊，所采用的数据来自一项由联邦政府资助、持续进行的美国老年人追踪调查“健康与退休研究”。研究人员通过综合认知测试来追踪受访者认知能力的变化，并以其步行速度来衡量身体功能，由于步行速度与身体功能障碍、住院及死亡风险密切相关，因此被视作一项重要的“生命体征”。

paragraphs.contentEn: Over a 12-year period, 45% of participants improved either mentally or physically. About 32% showed cognitive gains, while 28% improved physically, according to the study. "If you average everyone together, you see decline," Levy said. "But when you look at individual trajectories, you uncover a very different story. A meaningful percentage of the older participants … got better."
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究显示，在长达12年的追踪期内，45%的受访者在认知或身体功能方面出现改善。其中，约32%的人认知能力有所提升，28%的人身体状况得到改善。莱维表示：“如果把所有人的数据简单平均，整体看起来确实是在走下坡路。但一旦把目光转向个体的发展轨迹，就会发现一个截然不同的情况——相当一部分老年受访者的状况……实际上在变好。”

paragraphs.contentEn: A participant’s beliefs about aging appeared to influence the results, as those with more positive age beliefs were significantly more likely to show improvements in both cognition and walking speed. This remained true even after accounting for factors such as age, sex, education, chronic disease, depression and the length of follow-up. Improvements were seen even among participants who started with "normal" levels of function, not just those recovering from injuries or illness. "Individuals who have taken in more positive age beliefs ... tend to have a lower stress response and lower stress biomarkers," Levy said. Because age beliefs are modifiable, she noted, there could be a capacity for improvements later in life.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究发现，受访者对衰老的态度似乎会影响其结果，那些对衰老抱有更积极看法的人，其认知能力和步行速度出现改善的可能性显著更高。即使在控制了年龄、性别、教育水平、慢性病史、抑郁状况及随访时长等因素后，这一关联依然成立。值得注意的是，这种改善并非仅限于从伤病中恢复的人群，一些在研究开始时身体功能处于“正常”水平的参与者，其功能同样也出现了提升。莱维表示：“那些内化了更积极衰老观念的人……通常表现出较低的压力反应，其体内的压力生物标志物水平也更低。”她进一步强调，由于人们对衰老的看法是可以改变的，因此在晚年阶段仍然存在改善健康状况的可能性。

paragraphs.contentEn: The study did have some limitations, the researchers acknowledged. It didn’t look at how muscles or brain cells change and adapt, which could help explain why people improved. Future studies should examine improvement patterns for other types of cognition, such as spatial memory, they added. "In addition, although our participants were drawn from a nationally representative sample, it would be useful to examine patterns of improvement in additional cohorts that have a greater representation of different ethnic minority groups," the researchers noted in the study.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究人员承认，这项研究仍存在一定局限。研究并未探讨肌肉或脑细胞如何发生变化和适应，而这些机制或许有助于解释为何部分受访者的状况会出现改善。研究人员补充说，未来的研究还应考察其他类型认知能力的改善模式，例如空间记忆。研究团队在论文中写道：“此外，尽管本研究的受访者来自一个具有全国代表性的样本，但仍有必要在其他研究队列，尤其是那些包含更多不同少数族裔群体的样本中，对这种改善模式进行进一步的检验。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The authors said they hope the findings will debunk the myth that continuous physical and cognitive decline is inevitable. "We found evidence that there could be psychological pathways, behavioral pathways and physiological pathways [by which age beliefs impact health]," said Levy. "It’s common, and it should be included in our understanding of the aging process."
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究作者表示，他们希望这些发现有助于打破衰老必然伴随持续身心衰退的迷思。莱维指出：“我们的研究发现了一些证据，表明人们对衰老的看法可能通过心理、行为和生理等多种途径影响其健康。这些影响途径是普遍存在的，也应当被纳入我们对于衰老过程的理解之中。”
